observations.seen: Frames 1 to 3 hit a warm low-sun golden-hour key that fits the recipe. Building faces are mostly flat-lit with little bounce, though. In frame 4 (night) the street lamps and car cast no light pools, and no amber headlight glow is visible, so the scene reads as murky and uniformly dark.

Long building shadows cross the road in frames 1 and 3, but they are soft blobs with little definition. The car's contact shadow is weak, so the car floats slightly. Traffic lights, lamp posts and the taxi show no readable cast shadows.

The car's rear window shows a single blown-out sun hotspot with crackly noise around it in every day frame. The body paint has sparkly, noisy specular. The taxi in frame 2 has heavy speckled noise across its panels, which suggests an unfiltered or wrong-scale environment map.

The downtown canyon has repeated box towers with tiled window textures, plus traffic lights, lamps and palms. That is coherent but generic and repetitive. Frame 2's background hills are flat, untextured extruded blocks, and the street lacks clutter, signage and traffic density.

Warm distance haze fades the far end of the avenue in frames 1 to 3. Frame 2's background blocks sit in an orange murk that flattens depth instead of layering it. Frame 4 has almost no night atmosphere, with no light glow or fog falloff.

The road is a flat brown with no asphalt grain or wetness. Building facades are low-resolution flat textures. The car's license plate and rear bumper area are smeared, blurry texture patches, and the taxi texture is noisy.

The hero car and taxi are reasonably shaped. Buildings are simple boxes with painted-on windows, pedestrians are blocky low-poly figures, and the frame 2 hills are primitive extrusions. Asset fidelity is inconsistent between vehicles and the world.

The car is centered on the vanishing point, which gives strong one-point perspective down the avenue. In frames 1 and 2 the car fills only about 2 to 4% of the frame, well under the 15 to 25% target. In frames 3 and 4 it fills about 25 to 30% and blocks the road ahead.
The chase distance varies widely between frames 1/2 and frames 3/4. The camera height is low and level, with no visible speed cues like FOV kick or tilt at 101 km/h. Building edges show aliasing.

A warm grade is present, but there is no visible bloom on the sun, lamps or lit windows, and no film grain or vignette. Frame 3's orange sky clips. Edge aliasing and the blown car-window highlight show a weak tonemapping and AA pass.

A clean timer and ticket card, speedometer, nitro bar, score and minimap are legible in frames 1 and 2. In frames 3 and 4 the timer, ticket, score and nitro are missing and the speed readout has no number. The minimap is a dense, noisy grid that is hard to read.
